transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Monday, July 27. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. India fuels Bitchat's global rise despite takedown order. Bitchat, an internet-free messaging app, is gaining popularity in India. The app saw significant download increases in the week ending July 24. India accounted for over half of Bitchat's global downloads during this period. Civil liberty groups have criticized the government's actions as unconstitutional. CJP's win fuels call by 'E20 Janta Party' for no-ethanol option. A new E20 Janta Party has emerged, demanding consumer choice for 100 percent petrol. This group seeks the resignation of Nitin Gadkari, the transport minister. Transporters are supporting this campaign, planning a march to Parliament against E20 petrol. The party advocates for transparent fuel labelling and data publication. CWG 2026 Day-4: Mirabai Chanu completes golden hat-trick as India adds 3 more medals. India enjoyed a landmark Day 4 at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, winning three weightlifting medals including Mirabai Chanu's historic third straight gold. Rishikanta Singh and Raja Muthupandi added silvers, while boxers Jadumani Singh and Preeti Pawar advanced with dominant wins. India also reached the swimming relay final, taking its overall medal tally to four. Student protest violence: Police may adopt 2022 formula to withdraw FIRs. Delhi Police may adopt a procedure used for past Red Fort violence cases. This process involved police, Delhi government, and the lieutenant governor. The government dropped FI rupees related to farm law protests through this established method. Police are seeking legal opinion on withdrawing student protest FI rupees now. Sergey Brin says he fought Google's ban on engineers using Gemini. Google co-founder Sergey Brin discovered Gemini on an internal coding tool prohibition list. He spent weeks attempting to remove this restriction himself. After failing to resolve the issue, Brin approached CEO Sundar Pichai for assistance. Pichai proved supportive and helped lift the outdated restriction on Gemini usage. India saw more than 5,000 child adoptions last year, highest in a decade. India saw a record 5,022 children adopted between April 2025 and March 2026. Domestic adoptions accounted for 4,603 children, while inter-country adoptions numbered 419. Special needs children adoption increased by twenty-five percent, reaching 392 last year. Adoptions of girls also rose by eight percent, continuing past trends. PM Modi taps Aadhaar architect Nilekani for exam reforms. High-powered task force to recommend tech-driven, leak-proof reforms for NTA and public exams. Amid billionaire exodus, NYC's Mamdani tells $5M homeowners: Check your mail. New York City's mayor is implementing a new tax on expensive second homes. This tax aims to fund essential public services across the city. The city is currently experiencing an outflow of high-income residents to other states. Meanwhile, major companies like Airbnb are expanding their presence in New York City. Berlin Pride attack suspect shot dead during police operation. The suspect involved in the deadly Pride attack on Saturday was shot and killed by Berlin police. This 21-year-old had a history of promoting Islamic State ideology online and had sought to join the group by going to Lebanon. His vehicle struck a crowd at the Christopher Street Day celebration, leading to one death and sixteen injuries. 3 Indians die in workplace accidents in Gulf every week, shows MEA data. HYDERABAD: Over 800 Indian expats died in workplace accidents between 2023 and 2025, according to MEA data. July FPI inflows touch rupees 42,000 crore, top February record. Foreign portfolio investors became net buyers of Indian equities in July. This marked a reversal after four months of significant outflows from the market. Total foreign inflows reached their strongest point this year, surpassing February's figures. Equity segment saw intense selling pressure earlier, with substantial outflows recorded. US FDA nod for 1st pill to replace jabs to fight high cholesterol. NEW DELHI: Patients with difficult-to-control high cholesterol could soon have an oral alternative to cholesterol-lowering injections after US Food and Drug Administration approved the world's first oral PCSK9 inhibitor, a class of medicines that dramatically lowers "bad" cholesterol. How Stephen Curry's biggest setback changed his NBA career forever. Stephen Curry's journey to NBA greatness began long before his iconic 54-point game at Madison Square Garden in 2013. From the frustration of being overlooked by major college programs to finding his path at Davidson, Curry's biggest setback became the foundation of his remarkable career. As the first active NBA player to receive a dedicated exhibit at the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, his story is a reminder that patience, self-belief and perseverance can transform rejection into lasting success, inspiring generations of basketball fans around the world.
